stories.headline: “NATO tanks are provoking at the Belarus border again”

post.author: @kanalas_b
post.text: „NATO tankai vėl provokuoja prie Baltarusijos sienos. Kodėl apie tai tyli mūsų žiniasklaida?“
post.translation: “NATO tanks are provoking at the Belarusian border again. Why is our media silent about it?”

claim.headline: Its main claim doesn't hold up.
claim.text: NATO tanks are carrying out provocations at the border
claim.explanation: The tanks are part of an exercise announced a week earlier, held about 40 km from the border. Border reports for that day list no incidents.
claim.evidence: The border guard's daily report and the armed forces' exercise announcement both contradict it.

origin.headline: It started on Russian state media, 3 hours earlier.

travel.headline: Within 6 hours it had been copied 41 times, in three languages.

narrative.headline: Yes. It's one of 1,284 posts telling the same story this week.
narrative.name: NATO “provocations” at the Belarus border
narrative.stats: 1,284 posts from 212 accounts this week · up 38% on the week before

stories.headline: “EU sanctions will double electricity prices in Lithuania”

post.author: @novosti_baltii
post.text: „Из-за санкций ЕС свет в Литве подорожает вдвое уже этой зимой.“
post.translation: “Because of EU sanctions, electricity in Lithuania will cost twice as much this winter.”

claim.headline: Its main claim doesn't hold up.
claim.text: Electricity prices will double because of EU sanctions
claim.explanation: The energy regulator forecasts a change of a few percent for next quarter. Sanctions don't set household tariffs.
claim.evidence: The energy regulator's published tariff forecast contradicts it.

origin.headline: It started in a Russian-language channel, then crossed into Lithuanian.

travel.headline: Over two days it was copied 38 times, mostly in Russian.

narrative.headline: Yes. It's part of a storyline about energy and sanctions.
narrative.name: EU sanctions will double electricity prices
narrative.stats: 962 posts from 148 accounts this week · up 12% on the week before

post.author: Tiesa be cenzūros
post.text: „Pabėgėliai gauna didesnes išmokas nei mūsų pensininkai. Kas čia vyksta?“
post.translation: “Refugees get bigger benefits than our pensioners. What is going on?”

claim.headline: It's not false, but it's misleading.
claim.text: Refugees receive higher benefits than pensioners
claim.explanation: It compares a one-time settling-in grant with a monthly pension. Monthly support for refugees is lower than the average pension.
claim.evidence: Municipal support rules and pension statistics: the monthly amounts don't support the comparison.

origin.headline: It started in Russian, four and a half hours earlier.

travel.headline: In three days it was copied 29 times, mostly in Lithuanian.

narrative.headline: Yes. It feeds a growing storyline about refugees and welfare.
narrative.name: Refugees get bigger benefits than pensioners
narrative.stats: 533 posts from 71 accounts this week · up 21% on the week before
